entries.author: MyUncleSam
entries.reason: unzip in the PKGBUILD (extracting translations) plus 'bash -c' in the shipped wrapper script are combined across files into a decode-and-execute finding. Nothing is decoded and executed; the wrapper only starts the program.
entries.description: Seen with aur-scan 2.2.0 on CachyOS. The PKGBUILD only runs 'unzip' on the translation archive in prepare(); heidisql.install only prints notes; the wrapper 'heidisql' ends with '/bin/bash -c "exec -a $0 $EXEC $ARGS" "$0"'. The rule matches 'unzip' (decode) in one file and 'bash -c' (execute) in another.

entries.author: MyUncleSam
entries.reason: CRYPTO-003 matches a string inside the shipped binary package that only looks like a Monero/Bitcoin wallet address; DEEP-003 reports Unicode bidirectional control characters in the PKGBUILD. Both were analysed by Claude Sonnet, which found them harmless.
entries.description: Seen with aur-scan 2.2.0 on CachyOS. The package is a proprietary application shipped as a prebuilt archive; the 'wallet address' is a long string in the package file, not a payment address used by any code. The bidirectional characters in the PKGBUILD are part of normal text, not hidden code. The review of the package was performed by Claude Sonnet.
